goal: Three white ducks with orange beaks swim on the small pond in the park; Mia (drawn young, about five years old) kneels at the edge and points at them. No letters, words, or numbers anywhere.
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows four approved 3D children side by side, left to right: Pat, May, Sam, and Mia (ignore the gray background and the shadow; copy only the children). Picture 2 is the empty park set: green grass, a small round pond with stones and lily pads, a low tree, a sun and a blue sky; use it as the background and keep the same park. Picture 3 shows the small round pond with stones and lily pads (ignore the gray background). Picture 4 shows the white duck with an orange beak, from three sides (draw three of them). Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, chubby child hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Mia: light-brown shoulder-length hair with a small pink bow on the side, big brown eyes, a pink T-shirt, blue denim overalls, white shoes. The picture: Mia kneels at the edge of the pond and points at the ducks. A medium shot at a low camera height. The small round pond (picture 3) with its stones and lily pads fills the right two thirds of the picture; EXACTLY THREE white ducks with orange beaks (picture 4) swim on its water in a row, clearly separate from each other and clearly counted: three. Mia kneels on the green grass at the left edge of the pond, turned three quarters toward the ducks, and points at them with the index finger of her right hand; her other hand rests on her knee. She smiles with an open mouth. Soft green grass and the park background of picture 2 behind. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. The page text is "How many ducks? Three!" and is context only: do not draw any text.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, and the star. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the ground line, the pond as one closed oval with a few big closed stone shapes, the tree as one closed trunk shape with one closed cloud crown, the sun as one closed circle). No grass blades, no small leaves, no clover, no small flowers, no hatching, no tick marks, no wood grain lines, no cloud details. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes.
